Contract profiles

15 futures families retained from the supplied 3.0 source dataset.

CME

Nasdaq-100 E-mini · NQ / MNQ

Primary index-futures trade. High intraday range; NY activity is the main focus.

Open module →T1CME

S&P 500 E-mini · ES / MES

Primary index-futures trade and NQ comparison market. Often a smoother index tape than NQ, but this is a practitioner observation, not a guarantee.

Open module →T1COMEX

Gold · GC / MGC

Primary precious-metals trade; active in London and NY.

Open module →T1CME

Euro FX · 6E / M6E

Primary currency-futures trade; futures version of EUR/USD.

Open module →T1CME

British Pound · 6B / M6B

Primary currency-futures trade; London-focused and can show wide wicks.

Open module →T1CBOT

Dow E-mini · YM / MYM

Confirmation market for NQ/ES; not a default standalone ICT entry in this playbook.

Open module →T2CME

Russell 2000 · RTY / M2K

Small-cap and rate-sensitive confirmation market.

Open module →T2ICE US

US Dollar Index · DX

Dollar-bias instrument; use primarily for FX and gold context.

Open module →T2CBOT

10-Year T-Note · ZN

Treasury-price and yield context for rates-sensitive futures.

Open module →T2NYMEX

WTI Crude Oil · CL / MCL

Optional, news-driven energy contract.

Open module →T3CME

Japanese Yen · 6J

Optional currency-futures market for Asia/London research.

Open module →T3CME

Australian Dollar · 6A

Optional Asia-session FX future; sensitive to Australia and China.

Open module →T3CME

Canadian Dollar · 6C

Optional CAD future; oil and North American data can be relevant.

Open module →T3COMEX

Silver · SI / SIL

Optional precious metal; Gold comparison market and more volatile according to playbook convention.

Open module →T3CME

CME Bitcoin · BTC / MBT

Optional CME-regulated Bitcoin future; not equivalent to spot exchange BTC.

Open module →T3Metals

Gold · XAUUSD

Gold often reacts to real yields, the dollar, policy expectations and risk demand. Safe-haven flows can be offset by rising yields or USD strength.

Open module →Metals

Silver · XAGUSD

Silver combines precious-metal and industrial demand exposure; its volatility and liquidity can differ materially from Gold.

Open module →FX

EUR/USD

FX is relative: compare both central banks, growth/inflation surprises and yield spreads rather than analysing one currency alone.

Open module →FX

GBP/USD

Sterling reacts to UK policy and data versus US conditions. UK-specific political/fiscal headlines can change the transmission.

Open module →FX

USD/JPY

The yield differential and central-bank signals often matter, but intervention warnings and rapid carry unwinds can dominate short-term price action.

Open module →FX

USD/INR

INR can be influenced by oil import costs, dollar conditions, local flows and RBI actions. Confirm contract/venue eligibility with authorised sources.

Open module →FX

US Dollar Index · DXY

DXY is a currency benchmark, not a currency pair. Its composition and weights matter; strength does not mechanically force every asset lower.

Open module →Bonds & Rates

US 2-Year Treasury Yield

Short yields are especially sensitive to expected policy rates. Yield up usually means bond price down, but broader asset reactions depend on why yields moved.

Open module →Bonds & Rates

US 10-Year Treasury Yield

The 10-year reflects expected short rates plus term premium and other factors. Distinguish a growth-led rise from an inflation/fiscal-risk rise.

Open module →Bonds & Rates

US 30-Year Treasury Yield

Long bonds are sensitive to long-run inflation, supply/demand and term premium; duration risk can be substantial.

Open module →Equity Indices

S&P 500

Index direction combines earnings, rates, breadth and concentration. A few mega-caps can hide weak underlying breadth.

Open module →Equity Indices

Nasdaq-100

Long-duration growth stocks can be rate-sensitive, but earnings growth and positioning may dominate. Track semiconductor and mega-cap earnings separately.

Open module →Volatility

VIX Volatility Index

VIX is an implied-volatility measure, not a directional index or a directly tradable share. Futures/options have their own term structure and risks.

Open module →Indian Equities

Nifty 50

Indian equities combine earnings and global risk with INR, crude, domestic flows and index composition. Verify exchange notices and holidays.

Open module →Indian Equities

Nifty Bank

Bank indices are sensitive to rate transmission, deposit costs, loan growth and credit quality—not just the policy-rate decision.

Open module →Equity Indices

DAX · Germany

European equity performance can respond to ECB expectations, industrial cycle, energy costs and currency moves.

Open module →Equity Indices

Nikkei 225 · Japan

Export sensitivity and the yen can create meaningful cross-asset effects; track local-market hours and overnight US developments.

Open module →Energy

WTI Crude Oil

Oil prices reflect both physical balances and risk premium. An inventory draw can be bullish in one context and irrelevant if already expected.

Open module →Energy

Brent Crude

Brent has a global benchmark role; compare regional supply, freight/insurance risk and product-market spreads.

Open module →Energy

Natural Gas

Gas markets are highly regional and weather/seasonality sensitive. A contract benchmark may not reflect local retail gas prices.

Open module →Metals

Copper

Copper is often used as an industrial-cycle gauge, but inventory location, supply disruptions, currency and positioning can change the signal.

Open module →Metals

Aluminium

Aluminium is energy-intensive; power pricing, production restrictions and regional inventory flows can affect premiums and futures.

Open module →Battery Materials

Lithium / Battery Materials

Not every battery material has a liquid retail-tradable contract. Many prices are specialist assessments or private/physical agreements.

Open module →Crypto

Bitcoin · BTC

Crypto can trade 24/7 and react to liquidity, leverage and market-structure events. Exchange deposits alone do not prove an intent to sell.

Contract data quality rules

Tick size, tick value, multiplier, expiry, first notice and session hours are reference values only until independently reconciled with the official exchange specification and date-stamped. No broker margin is inferred.
